This looks like two different things collected together: the 42 and 42 copies split into groups differing by 0.19 in identity to the consensus (his mixtures run 0.13-0.22, single families 0.01-0.12). Median lengths are 36 and 0 bp. Separate them and re-run each part - the score is withheld, because scoring a mixture answers neither question.

17 % of the flank sits inside patches of raised similarity (426 columns in 49 patches), yet the flank average is an ordinary 0.27. The similarity is localised, so averaging hides it. Some copies are probably inside a shared larger repeat or duplication: worth checking those flanks against the whole genome before treating every copy as an independent insertion.

The sequence flanking these copies is itself shared (identity 0.73 at the edge, reaching background only 100 bp out). They look like fragments of a longer element — a LINE 3' end or similar — rather than a short element with its own boundaries.
22 % of the flank sits inside patches of raised similarity (424 columns in 38 patches), which agrees with the raised flank average of 0.45.

Only 2 of 68 copies form the core the consensus is actually built on (3 %). The rest are too divergent or too truncated to support it, so the score describes a minority of what was collected. Look at whether the other 66 belong here at all.

34 % of the element is simple tandem repeat in the median copy (86 % in the top tenth). Every family Sergei accepted in hydra sits at or below 7 %, and no class in the labelled corpus reaches 1 %. A consensus built mostly out of microsatellite will collect loci by their repeat content, not by common descent.

25 % of the flanking sequence is simple tandem repeat in the median copy. The copies are sitting in microsatellite tracts, so the flanks cannot show whether the insertions are independent and short-read mapping into such tracts is unreliable.

The copies support consensus positions 250-310 (identity 0.88) much better than the consensus as a whole (0.60). Coverage is even across the full length, so the copies are present at the ends and simply do not match there - the consensus is longer than the element it describes. Trim it to that window and re-run; the family is real, the boundary is not.
